introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Pure Mathematics With Statistics, Paper 3 (0770/3), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Time allowed: THREE HOURS.**

Full marks may be obtained for answers to ALL questions. Mathematical formulae and tables produced by the GCE Board are allowed. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving the answer at each stage. Electronic calculators are allowed. Start each question on a fresh page.
enonce_intro_markdown:
The probability density function $f$, of a continuous random variable $X$, is defined by

$$f(x) = \begin{cases} kx(4 - x^2), & 0 \le x \le 3, \\ 0, & \text{elsewhere.} \end{cases}$$
incertitudes: Question 6 (sujet imprimé défectueux) : avec $k = -\frac{4}{9}$, imposé par la partie (a), la fonction $f(x) = kx(4 - x^2)$ est NÉGATIVE sur $0 < x < 2$ : ce n'est donc pas une vraie densité, et la moyenne trouvée en (b), $\frac{28}{5} = 5.6$, est hors de l'intervalle $[0, 3]$. Les trois parties (a), (b), (c) restent cohérentes entre elles (l'équation de (c) découle bien de $k = -\frac{4}{9}$) : elles sont traitées telles qu'imprimées, comme calculs algébriques, et le corrigé signale le défaut dans une remarque.
Question 6 : les points imprimés par partie, (5, 5, 3), totalisent 13 ; recopiés tels quels.
Question 6 (a) : le sujet imprime « $k = -\frac{4}{9}$ » avec le signe moins ; l'énoncé est recopié ainsi (le calcul de l'intégrale donne bien $\frac{-9}{4}\, k = 1$, soit $k = -\frac{4}{9}$).

questions.enonce_markdown: (a) Show that the value of the constant $k$ is $-\dfrac{4}{9}$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
For $f$ to be a probability density function, the total probability is 1:

$$\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)\,dx = \int_0^3 kx(4 - x^2)\,dx = 1$$

$$k\int_0^3 (4x - x^3)\,dx = k\left[2x^2 - \frac{x^4}{4}\right]_0^3 = k\left(18 - \frac{81}{4}\right) = k\left(-\frac{9}{4}\right)$$

So $-\dfrac{9}{4}\,k = 1$, which gives

$$k = -\frac{4}{9}$$

as required.

*Remark.* With $k = -\dfrac{4}{9}$ the function $f(x) = -\dfrac{4}{9}x(4 - x^2)$ is negative for $0 < x < 2$ (where $4 - x^2 > 0$), so the printed $f$ is not a genuine density. The question is answered as set: the value $k = -\dfrac{4}{9}$ is what the normalisation condition produces.

$$E(X) = \int_0^3 x\,f(x)\,dx = k\int_0^3 (4x^2 - x^4)\,dx = k\left[\frac{4x^3}{3} - \frac{x^5}{5}\right]_0^3$$

$$E(X) = k\left(36 - \frac{243}{5}\right) = k\left(-\frac{63}{5}\right) = \left(-\frac{4}{9}\right)\left(-\frac{63}{5}\right) = \frac{28}{5}$$

**$E(X) = \dfrac{28}{5} = 5.6$.**

*Remark.* As noted in (a), the printed $f$ is not a true density, which is why this "mean" lies outside $[0, 3]$; the value is the one the printed definition gives.

questions.enonce_markdown: (c) If the upper quartile of the random variable $X$ is $q$, show that $4q^4 - 32q^2 - 27 = 0$.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The upper quartile $q$ is the value with $P(X \le q) = \dfrac{3}{4}$. For $0 \le q \le 3$:

$$P(X \le q) = \int_0^q kx(4 - x^2)\,dx = k\left[2x^2 - \frac{x^4}{4}\right]_0^q = k\left(2q^2 - \frac{q^4}{4}\right)$$

With $k = -\dfrac{4}{9}$:

$$-\frac{4}{9}\left(2q^2 - \frac{q^4}{4}\right) = \frac{3}{4} \iff -\frac{8q^2}{9} + \frac{q^4}{9} = \frac{3}{4}$$

Multiplying both sides by $36$:

$$-32q^2 + 4q^4 = 27 \iff 4q^4 - 32q^2 - 27 = 0$$

as required.

*Note.* The equation is a quadratic in $q^2$: $q^2 = \dfrac{32 + \sqrt{1456}}{8} \approx 8.77$ (the other root is negative), so $q \approx 2.96$, which does lie in $[0, 3]$.
